Today is **April 17, 2026**, so in Quzhou my **winter wheat is already in the field**. I will treat this as my **2026 farming plan**: finish managing the current wheat, harvest it in June, then plant summer maize right after, and plant the next wheat crop in **early October 2026** for the following harvest.

I farm 16.9 mu, and there are only 2 people in the household, with some off-farm work, so I cannot make things too complicated. I have farmed here a long time, and around here wheat-maize is still the safest way. The extension guy says not to overdo nitrogen, but from my own fields, if wheat looks weak and I save too much on fertilizer, yield drops fast. So I will stay with a moderate rate, a bit careful on cost but not too low. For wheat, I will keep one base fertilizer and one topdressing, and irrigate at the key stages because well water costs money, but skipping water at jointing or grain filling is risky. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is very tight, so I will use simple field prep and plant quickly, probably with a hybrid seed that most people nearby use. I will not chase very high input because labor is short and cash must be kept in hand, but I also do not want to cut too much and lose yield. That is how I usually balance it.
